reception.text: The Morning Oregonian ran the Senate call on page one under "EXTRA SESSION CALLED," printing the proclamation in full.

political_impact.text: The Senate met in executive session from March 5 to March 19, 1903, to act on the canal treaty with Colombia and the Cuban commercial convention.
political_impact.source: Roosevelt, message to the Senate, Mar. 5, 1903

political_impact.text: The Senate consented to the Hay–Herrán canal treaty without change, by a vote reported as 73 to 5.
After days of amendment fights the Senate consented to the Cuban convention, 50 to 16, adding that it would not take effect until approved by Congress.
political_impact.source: United States v. American Sugar Refining Co., 202 U.S. 563 (1906); Morning Oregonian

legacy.text: Colombia's Senate rejected the Hay–Herrán treaty, and the Panama crisis of November 1903 followed.

related.note: The Senate amendment adopted in this session made the November call of the whole Congress necessary.

reception.text: The Morning Oregonian headlined "EXTRA SESSION / President Calls Congress to Meet November 9," printing the full text.
The Los Angeles Herald noted of the House vote on the Cuban bill: "There Was No Record Vote."

political_impact.text: The House adopted a special rule fixing the time of the vote, 183 to 160, with six Republicans from Michigan and Colorado voting with the Democrats against it.
political_impact.source: Voteview, House roll calls 3–5, 58th Congress; Morning Oregonian, Nov. 17, 1903

political_impact.text: The House passed the Cuban reciprocity bill by a rising vote of 335 to 21, with no names recorded.
political_impact.source: San Francisco Call, Nov. 20, 1903 (AP); Press Democrat (Santa Rosa), Nov. 20, 1903

political_impact.text: The Senate talked the bill past the end of the special session, which merged into the regular session on December 7, then passed it 57 to 18 on December 16.
political_impact.source: Voteview, Senate roll call 1, 58th Congress; Congressional Record vol. 38, p. 286

political_impact.text: Roosevelt signed the bill on December 17, 1903; it became chapter 1 of the regular second session.

legacy.text: The Cuban convention took effect on December 27, 1903, and bound the Cuban and American sugar trades closely together for the next three decades.
legacy.source: United States v. American Sugar Refining Co., 202 U.S. 563 (1906)

related.note: The March Senate session added the requirement of congressional approval.
Cuban copyright proclamation signed eight days into this session.
